questions.q: What problem does Snowpipe solve that manual COPY INTO doesn't handle well?
options: Files landing continuously and unpredictably, without someone scheduling or triggering each load by hand
Loading files larger than 1 GB
Loading data into more than one table at once
Converting CSV files into Parquet automatically
questions.explain: Snowpipe is event-driven, reacting to new files automatically — ideal for continuous, unpredictable arrivals rather than scheduled batches.

questions.q: What are the two ways a Snowpipe load can be triggered?
options: Cloud storage event notifications (e.g. S3 ObjectCreated) or the Snowpipe REST API's insertFiles call
A CRON schedule or a manual button click in Snowsight
A stored procedure or a user-defined function
A warehouse resize event or a role change
questions.explain: Snowpipe supports triggering via cloud storage events or by directly calling its REST API from your own application.

questions.q: What does a pipe's body actually contain?
options: The same COPY INTO statement already covered in Chapter 3 — stages, file formats, and ON_ERROR all still apply
A completely new loading language unrelated to COPY INTO
Only a file path, with no SQL involved
A CREATE TABLE statement
questions.explain: A pipe wraps an existing COPY INTO statement and adds an automatic trigger — it introduces no new load syntax.

questions.q: What does AUTO_INGEST = TRUE do on a pipe?
options: Ties the pipe to cloud storage event notifications so it runs automatically when a new file arrives
Forces the pipe to reload every file every hour
Disables error handling on the pipe
Converts the pipe into a scheduled task
questions.explain: AUTO_INGEST = TRUE connects the pipe to the cloud storage event notification mechanism described in this lesson.

questions.q: What does "serverless" mean in the context of Snowpipe's compute model?
options: Snowflake provisions and bills compute for the pipe's loads separately — you never assign it a warehouse or size it yourself
The load runs with zero compute resources at all
It only works without any internet connection
It requires you to manually start and stop a server
questions.explain: Serverless here means Snowflake-managed compute specific to the pipe's loads, billed per-second/per-file, distinct from your interactive warehouses.
